# QSBS Facts

> Data-driven analysis of Section 1202 Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS) tax policy. Argues against state-level QSBS decoupling using U.S. Treasury data, academic studies, and migration statistics.

URL: https://qsbsfacts.org

## What This Site Covers

QSBS Facts presents evidence-based analysis of IRC Section 1202 — the federal tax exclusion for qualified small business stock. The site counters the narrative that QSBS is a "tax loophole for millionaires" by examining actual Treasury data on who claims the exclusion, how often, and how much.

## Key Data Points (U.S. Treasury OTA Working Paper 127, January 2025)

- **75% of QSBS claimants** used the exclusion exactly once across 11 years (2012–2022). Only 6% claimed it five or more years.
- **74% of claimants** earn under $1 million (by average income, excluding QSBS gains). The largest group (35%) earns $100K–$400K.
- **Median annual exclusion: $2,810.** 90th percentile is $590,940. This is not a large-dollar benefit for most claimants.
- **QSBS was 2.55% of all capital gains** in 2021 — a rounding error in total capital gains activity.
- **$152 billion** in total exclusions claimed from 2012–2022, peaking at $51.1B in 2021.
- **The "94% goes to millionaires" claim** (from ITEP) combines two groups: 74% of dollars going to people already over $1M, and 20% going to people whose one-time exit temporarily pushed them over $1M. The second group is exactly who QSBS was designed for.

## Academic Evidence

- Edwards & Todenhaupt (2020): Startup investment increased ~12% after the 100% exclusion was enacted in 2010.
- Chen & Farre-Mensa (2023/2025): QSBS-eligible industries experienced more firm births, more startup employment, and increased first-round VC.
- Critics (Mitchell/Equitable Growth 2023; Pomerleau & Mitchell AEI/Tax Notes Oct 2025; Shilov/Tax Foundation Dec 2025) argue cost-effectiveness and complexity. Those papers do not measure the 2010 100% expansion the way the two studies above do. State decoupling does not repeal the federal incentive.

## Federal rules (P.L. 119-21 §70431, signed July 4, 2025)

Qualifying stock acquired on or before July 4, 2025 generally requires more than five years, with a $10M baseline eligible-gain limit or the 10× basis alternative. Stock acquired after that date uses at-least-3/4/5-year exclusion tiers (50/75/100%) and a $15M baseline limit, with coordination and prior-use rules. The $75M gross-asset threshold applies to stock issued after July 4, 2025. The newer dollar limit and asset threshold are indexed after 2026. See the educational guides for details and primary law. JCT (JCX-35-25) scores a small near-term revenue gain through 2028, then −$17.2B over 2025–34.

## Migration Data (IRS SOI 2021–2022)

- Top states gaining tax filers: FL (+125,551), TX (+88,216), NC (+43,653), SC (+32,927), TN (+30,935)
- Top states losing tax filers: CA (-144,203), NY (-108,586), IL (-45,460), MA (-26,033), NJ (-20,820)
- California lost $102 billion in AGI to outmigration from 2020–2022. California never conformed and still hosts the largest U.S. venture cluster; the 2026 lesson for other states is New York keeping QSBS, not California 2013.

## State Conformity (September 2026)

31 jurisdictions conform, 8 have no income tax, 8 are decoupled (AL, CA, DC, IL, MS, OR, PA, RI — RI effective 2027), 4 have partial conformity (HI 50% frozen pre-OBBBA; MA follows IRC as of Jan 1, 2024; ME decoupled only for stock acquired after July 3, 2025; VT add-back with 40% CG exclusion cap $350k). No pending states. New York rejected decoupling (FY2027 budget, May 28, 2026). Washington SB 6229 and Maryland HB 801 failed. New Jersey full conformity is in force for 2026+.

## Trust stacking

Treasury WP-127: $6.65B (13%) of 2021 QSBS exclusions flowed through trusts, up from nearly nothing in 2012. The site's reform line: cap or disallow multiplied exclusions through related nongrantor trusts; do not tax the median $2,810 claim to do it.

## Pages

- **Homepage** (https://qsbsfacts.org): Full single-page analysis with all sections, charts, and interactive calculator.
- **Evidence** (https://qsbsfacts.org/evidence/): Academic evidence that QSBS drives startup formation and investment. Edwards & Todenhaupt (2020), Chen & Farre-Mensa (2023/2025).
- **Who Uses It** (https://qsbsfacts.org/who-uses-it/): Treasury data on claimant demographics, income levels, exclusion amounts, and the 4 archetypes.
- **The 94% Claim** (https://qsbsfacts.org/the-94-percent-claim/): Deconstruction of the ITEP "94% goes to millionaires" methodology and the dollar-weighted vs. people-counted distinction.
- **Calculator** (https://qsbsfacts.org/calculator/): Interactive exit tax calculator for all 50 states + DC. Supports URL parameter sharing.
- **State Impact** (https://qsbsfacts.org/state-impact/): State conformity map, IRS migration data, and California's $102B AGI loss from outmigration.
- **Sources** (https://qsbsfacts.org/sources/): All citations, data sources, methodology notes, and links to primary documents.


## Educational guides

[Browse all guides](https://qsbsfacts.org/guides/). These explain general rules and link to primary sources; they do not establish personal tax eligibility or residency.

- [What is qualified small business stock?](https://qsbsfacts.org/what-is-qsbs/): A plain-English introduction to Section 1202 and how the exclusion works.
- [Does my stock qualify for QSBS?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-eligibility/): Work through the company, shareholder, and stock requirements before relying on an exclusion.
- [How long do I need to hold QSBS?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-holding-period/): Compare holding periods and understand which acquisition dates control the rules.
- [How much gain can I exclude?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-exclusion-limits/): Understand the dollar caps, the basis alternative, and the limits of a simplified example.
- [What changed in the QSBS rules?](https://qsbsfacts.org/new-qsbs-rules/): Compare the older rules with the changes enacted in July 2025.
- [Can employee stock options lead to QSBS?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-stock-options/): Distinguish an option grant, acquiring shares, compensation, and a later stock sale.
- [What is a Section 1045 rollover?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-rollover/): Understand replacement stock, the election, and how deferral differs from exclusion.
- [What is QSBS trust stacking?](https://qsbsfacts.org/qsbs-trust-stacking/): An explanation of taxpayer limits, trust structures, and the policy debate.
- [California QSBS and state taxes](https://qsbsfacts.org/california-qsbs/): Understand California treatment and the questions a move before a sale raises.
- [Moving out of California before an exit](https://qsbsfacts.org/california-exit-tax/): Understand residency, income sourcing, and why a day count cannot answer every case.
- [Oregon QSBS after SB 1507](https://qsbsfacts.org/oregon-qsbs/): Read about enacted state changes, effective dates, and the discussion about future reform.
- [New York QSBS and state conformity](https://qsbsfacts.org/new-york-qsbs/): Understand New York treatment and distinguish budget proposals from enacted rules.
